blocks.x: DIY Epoxy Flooring vs Professional Installation: Is It Worth the Risk?

Walk into any DIY store and you'll find epoxy floor paint kits promising a showroom-quality finish for under £100. It's tempting. But there's a reason professional epoxy flooring costs more, and it's not just about the materials. The difference between a DIY job and a professional installation is the difference between a floor that lasts months versus one that lasts decades.
The DIY Epoxy Kit: What You're Really Buying

Most retail epoxy kits contain water-based epoxy (not 100% solids epoxy), a small quantity of decorative flakes, and basic application tools. The epoxy itself is typically much thinner than professional-grade material, it's essentially a heavy-duty floor paint with some epoxy content. While it will look decent immediately after application, it lacks the build thickness, chemical resistance, and bond strength of a professional system.
The #1 Cause of DIY Epoxy Failure: Surface Preparation

This cannot be overstated. Poor surface preparation is the single biggest cause of epoxy floor failure, and it's the step most DIY kits skip entirely or handle inadequately. Professional epoxy installation requires diamond grinding the concrete surface using industrial machinery. This creates a surface profile (similar to sandpaper) that the epoxy can mechanically bond to. Without this, the epoxy is effectively sitting on top of the concrete rather than bonding into it.

A DIY kit will typically suggest acid etching as an alternative. While acid etching is better than nothing, it doesn't create the same bond profile as diamond grinding. It also introduces moisture into the concrete, which can cause the epoxy to delaminate later. Worse, acid etching requires careful handling of hazardous materials and proper neutralisation and rinsing, steps that are often rushed or skipped.
Moisture: The Silent Killer

Concrete is porous and contains moisture. Before applying epoxy, professional installers test for moisture content and vapour transmission. If moisture levels are too high and epoxy is applied anyway, the moisture will push the coating off the concrete from underneath, a process called delamination. DIY kits rarely include moisture testing equipment, and most homeowners don't know this step is necessary.
Common DIY Failure Points

Even if preparation is adequate, DIY applications face several challenges. Hot tyre pickup: Water-based epoxy can soften when hot tyres sit on it, causing the coating to peel. Professional 100% solids epoxy is far more resistant. Inconsistent thickness: Achieving a uniform coating thickness with a roller is difficult. Thin spots wear through quickly. UV yellowing: Most DIY kits don't include a UV-stable top coat. Epoxy naturally yellows in sunlight, which is why professional systems include a polyurethane or polyaspartic top coat. Bubbles and pinholes: Outgassing from concrete can create bubbles that pop and leave pinholes. Professionals use primer coats and spike rolling techniques to manage this.
The True Cost of a Failed DIY Floor

Here's the scenario we see regularly: someone spends a weekend and £150 on a DIY epoxy kit. It looks good for 6-12 months. Then the edges start lifting near the garage door. Hot tyres cause peeling where the car parks. The floor yellows where sunlight hits. Within 18 months, the floor looks terrible. Now they call us to strip the failed coating and start over.

The cost to remove a failed DIY epoxy floor is significant, it requires heavy grinding to remove all the old coating, more work than preparing a bare concrete floor. The total cost ends up being the professional installation cost plus the cost of removing the failed DIY job. The "cheap" DIY option has become the most expensive route.
Lifespan Comparison

A professionally installed epoxy floor using industrial-grade materials typically lasts 15-25+ years in a residential garage. A DIY epoxy floor typically lasts 1-3 years before showing significant wear, peeling, or discolouration. That's a 10x difference in lifespan for what might be a 3-4x difference in upfront cost, making professional installation the better value over time.
When DIY Might Be OK

If you're coating a shed floor, a rarely-used workshop, or a utility room that won't see vehicle traffic or heavy use, a DIY kit might be adequate. But for a garage that will have cars parked on it, a commercial space, or anywhere you want the floor to look good and last, professional installation is the only sensible choice. blocks.x: How Much Does Epoxy Flooring Cost in the UK? (2026 Price Guide)

If you're considering epoxy flooring for your garage, commercial unit, or industrial space, one of the first questions you'll ask is: "How much does it cost?" The answer depends on several factors, floor size, condition, the system you choose, and the level of preparation required. This guide breaks down everything you need to know about UK epoxy flooring costs in 2026.
Typical Epoxy Flooring Costs in the UK

At Rhino Coating we quote every floor individually. Rather than publish a headline figure that will not hold true across different slabs and systems, we price from a survey: floor area, slab condition, the system chosen and the preparation required. Your quotation includes the complete installation, preparation, materials and labour, not just materials. It reflects the industrial-grade resins, the diamond grinding and the professional installation that goes into every floor. Call 07822 032335 for a figure on your own garage.

It's important to understand what you're paying for. You can find "epoxy floor paint" at DIY stores for under £20 per square metre, but these are fundamentally different products from the commercial-grade systems used by professional installers. A tin of garage floor paint will not deliver the same durability, finish, or longevity as a professionally installed multi-layer epoxy system.
Factors That Affect the Cost of Epoxy Flooring
1. Floor Size

The most obvious factor, larger floors require more materials and labour. A standard single garage (approximately 15-18m²) will cost less than a double garage (30-36m²), which in turn costs less than an industrial unit spanning hundreds of square metres. However, there are economies of scale: the cost per square metre often decreases slightly for larger projects because setup costs are spread across a bigger area.
2. Floor Condition and Preparation

This is the single biggest variable. A brand-new concrete floor in good condition requires less preparation than an old, oil-stained garage floor with cracks and spalling. Proper preparation, including diamond grinding, is essential for adhesion and cannot be skipped. If your floor has significant damage, oil contamination, or requires crack repairs, the preparation cost increases accordingly.
3. The Epoxy System You Choose

Different systems have different material costs. Our Rhino HB-200 solid colour system provides a durable, seamless finish suitable for most garages and workshops. The Rhino FB-400 full flake system involves broadcasting decorative flakes into the wet epoxy, creating a multi-colour, textured finish that hides imperfections and looks premium. The Rhino M-Flow marble effect system creates stunning, one-of-a-kind patterns using multiple colours swirled together, the most labour-intensive and highest-end option.
4. Geographic Location

Where you are in the UK can affect the final price. Labour and transport costs vary by region, and projects in cities like London may carry a small premium compared to other areas. We serve all major UK cities, from London and Manchester to Glasgow and beyond.
5. Additional Features

Coving (a curved edge where the floor meets the wall), anti-slip additives, logo inlays, or colour matching can all add to the final cost. These are optional upgrades that enhance functionality or aesthetics depending on your needs.
Why Professional Epoxy Flooring Costs More, and Why It's Worth It

A common question is: "Why does professional epoxy flooring cost more than a DIY kit?" The answer lies in what you're actually getting. Professional installation includes industrial diamond grinding to create the correct surface profile for adhesion, moisture testing to prevent future delamination, commercial-grade epoxy resins (not watered-down retail products), UV-stable polyurethane or polyaspartic top coats, and a written warranty that stands behind the work.

A DIY kit from a hardware store might cost £60-£150 for materials, but if the preparation isn't done correctly, and it rarely is without professional equipment, the floor can fail within months. The cost of stripping a failed DIY floor and having it professionally redone is far higher than doing it right the first time.
Finance Options

We offer 12 months interest-free finance on all epoxy flooring installations. This means you can spread the cost of your new floor over a full year with no additional charges, making a premium installation more accessible.
Get an Accurate Quote

blocks.x: Epoxy vs Polyurethane Flooring: What's the Difference?

When researching resin flooring, two terms come up constantly: epoxy and polyurethane. While they're both used in professional flooring systems, they serve different purposes and have distinct properties. Understanding the difference is key to choosing the right floor for your space.
What Is Epoxy Flooring?

Epoxy is a thermosetting polymer that cures through a chemical reaction between resin and hardener. Once cured, it forms an extremely hard, durable surface with exceptional adhesion to concrete. Epoxy's key properties include very high compressive strength, excellent chemical resistance, superb adhesion to properly prepared concrete, and the ability to be applied in thick layers (high build).

Epoxy forms the foundation of professional resin flooring systems. It's what bonds to your concrete and provides the structural strength of the floor. At Rhino Coating, our Rhino HB-200, FB-400, and M-Flow systems all use epoxy as the primary build layer.
What Is Polyurethane Flooring?

Polyurethane is a different type of polymer that offers properties epoxy doesn't. Polyurethane is more flexible than epoxy, it can absorb impact and movement without cracking. It's highly UV stable, meaning it won't yellow or chalk when exposed to sunlight. It also has good abrasion resistance and chemical resistance.

However, polyurethane doesn't bond as strongly to concrete as epoxy does, which is why it's generally not used as a base layer directly on concrete. Instead, it's most commonly used as a protective top coat over an epoxy base.
The Key Difference: Epoxy Base, Polyurethane Top Coat

The best professional flooring systems, including all of ours at Rhino Coating, combine both materials. An epoxy base layer provides the strong bond to concrete, high build thickness, and compressive strength. A UV-stable polyurethane or polyaspartic top coat provides protection from sunlight, flexibility to prevent cracking from temperature changes, and resistance to yellowing and wear.
This is like a car's bodywork and clear coat. The epoxy is the structural component (the bodywork), and the polyurethane is the protective finish (the clear coat).
When to Use Each
Epoxy is best for:

Garages and workshops (high compressive strength for vehicle loads), commercial kitchens (excellent chemical resistance), industrial floors (heavy equipment and forklift traffic), and any application requiring a thick, durable build layer.
Polyurethane is ideal for:

Floors exposed to direct sunlight (UV stability prevents yellowing), areas with temperature fluctuations (flexibility prevents cracking), and as a protective top coat over epoxy systems. It's also well-suited for food processing facilities and healthcare environments.
Polyaspartic: The Modern Alternative

Polyaspartic coatings are a type of polyurethane that cure faster and can be applied at lower temperatures. They offer similar UV stability and flexibility but with quicker turnaround times. At Rhino Coating, we offer polyaspartic top coats as an option for projects where faster curing is beneficial.
What About Water-Based Epoxy?

You may encounter water-based epoxy products in DIY stores. These are fundamentally different from the 100% solids epoxy used by professionals. Water-based epoxies are thinner, less durable, and not suitable for garage or commercial floors that need to withstand real use. They're essentially floor paint with some epoxy content, not a true epoxy flooring system.
The Rhino Coating Approach

Every Rhino Coating system uses an epoxy base for strength and adhesion with a UV-stable polyurethane or polyaspartic top coat for lasting protection. This gives you the best of both materials: the durability of epoxy combined with the UV resistance and flexibility of polyurethane. Get in touch to discuss which system is right for your project, or call 07822 032335.

blocks.x: Garage Flooring Ideas: Epoxy Colours & Finishes Compared

Choosing the right finish for your epoxy floor isn't just about looks, different systems suit different environments, budgets, and aesthetic preferences. Here's a complete comparison of the three Rhino Coating epoxy flooring systems to help you decide.
Rhino HB-200: Solid High Build Epoxy System

The HB-200 is our solid colour epoxy system, clean, seamless, and professional. It's applied in a single solid colour of your choice and finished with a UV-stable top coat. The result is a smooth, glossy, uniform surface that looks modern and understated.

Best for: Garages where you want a clean, functional finish without decorative elements. Workshops and commercial spaces where a professional, no-nonsense appearance is preferred. Budget-conscious projects that still demand professional-grade durability.

Colour options: Choose from a range of solid colours including light grey, mid grey, dark grey, beige, and more. The solid colour creates a bright, clean surface that reflects light well, excellent for making garages feel larger and brighter.

Key benefits: Excellent light reflection (brightens the space), easy to keep clean (smooth surface sweeps and mops easily), classic, timeless appearance that won't date. The most affordable of our three systems while still using industrial-grade materials.
Rhino FB-400: Full Flake Broadcast System

The FB-400 is our most popular system, and it's easy to see why. Coloured vinyl flakes are broadcast (scattered) into wet epoxy, creating a multi-colour, textured finish that's both decorative and practical. The flakes are then sealed with a clear top coat for a smooth, glossy surface.

Best for: Homeowners who want their garage to look as good as the rest of the house. Show garages where appearance matters as much as durability. Commercial spaces like car showrooms, retail units, or hospitality venues where a premium aesthetic is important.

Colour and flake options: Flake blends are available in numerous colour combinations, from subtle grey, white and black blends to bold blues, reds, and custom colour mixes. The flake finish hides minor imperfections in the concrete and disguises dust and tyre marks better than a solid colour.

Key benefits: Premium, decorative appearance. Hides minor surface imperfections and dust. Excellent slip resistance (the flake texture provides natural grip). The most popular choice for residential garages and showrooms.
Rhino M-Flow: Marble Effect System

The M-Flow is our premium designer system. Multiple colours of epoxy are poured and manipulated on the floor to create flowing, marble-like patterns. Each floor is completely unique, no two M-Flow installations look the same. The result is a stunning, high-end finish that transforms the space.

Best for: Luxury residential garages and showrooms. High-end retail and hospitality spaces. Anywhere you want the floor to be a genuine feature, not just a surface. Clients who want something truly bespoke and one-of-a-kind.

Colour options: You choose the colour palette, from classic white and grey marble effects to dramatic dark tones with metallic accents. The colours are swirled and blended during installation by our experienced installers to create natural-looking patterns.

Key benefits: Genuinely unique, no two floors are the same. Stunning, high-end appearance that transforms any space. Excellent at hiding dirt and marks (the natural pattern disguises imperfections). The premium choice for those who want the very best.
Comparing the Three Systems
Which System Is Right for You?

The right choice depends on your priorities. If you want a functional, clean garage floor at the most accessible price point, the HB-200 is your system. If you want the premium look that most people associate with a "show garage" and excellent practicality, the FB-400 is the most popular choice for good reason. If you're looking for something truly exceptional, a floor that's as much a feature as any car or display, the M-Flow delivers a genuinely unique result.

All three systems use the same industrial-grade preparation process, epoxy base, and UV-stable top coat. The difference is in the decorative layer. Whichever you choose, you're getting a floor built to last decades. Request a free quote or call 07822 032335 to discuss your project and see samples.

blocks.x: How Long Does Epoxy Flooring Last? A Realistic Lifespan Guide

One of the most common questions we hear is: "How long will my epoxy floor last?" The honest answer depends on several factors, the quality of the installation, the environment it's in, and how well it's maintained. Here's a realistic guide to what you can expect.
Residential Epoxy Flooring Lifespan: 15-25+ Years

A professionally installed epoxy floor in a residential garage can last 15-25 years or more. In many cases, the floor will outlast your ownership of the property. Residential garages see relatively light use, a car or two, some DIY projects, and foot traffic. With proper care, a high-quality epoxy floor in this environment should look good and perform well for decades.

We've seen Rhino Coating floors that are still in excellent condition after 15+ years of regular use. The key is professional installation with proper diamond ground preparation, industrial-grade materials, and a UV-stable top coat.
Commercial Epoxy Flooring Lifespan: 10-15+ Years

Commercial environments place more demands on flooring. Forklift traffic, heavy equipment, chemical spills, and constant foot traffic all contribute to wear. A well-installed commercial epoxy floor typically lasts 10-15+ years in these conditions, though heavy industrial use may reduce this to 7-10 years before recoating is needed.
Commercial environments benefit from regular maintenance and occasional re-application of the top coat, which can extend the floor's life significantly without the need for a full replacement.
What Affects Epoxy Floor Longevity?
1. Installation Quality

This is the single biggest factor. A floor that has been properly prepared, diamond ground, moisture tested, and primed, will last far longer than one where these steps were skipped. Professional installation using industrial-grade epoxy systems will dramatically outlast a DIY job. This cannot be overstated: preparation determines lifespan.
2. UV Exposure

Epoxy naturally yellows when exposed to UV light. This doesn't affect the structural integrity of the floor, but it does affect appearance. A UV-stable polyurethane or polyaspartic top coat, which all Rhino Coating systems include, prevents this yellowing. Floors without a UV-stable top coat (including most DIY jobs) will discolour within 1-2 years if exposed to sunlight.
3. Usage and Traffic

A garage that houses a single classic car and sees occasional use will wear differently from a busy commercial workshop. Heavy point loading (from jacks, stands, or machinery feet), dragging heavy items across the floor, and chemical spills all accelerate wear. Being mindful of how you use the floor, using protective mats under heavy equipment, cleaning up spills promptly, makes a difference.
4. Maintenance

Epoxy floors are relatively low-maintenance, but they're not maintenance-free. Regular sweeping to remove grit (which acts like sandpaper underfoot), occasional damp mopping, and avoiding harsh chemicals will keep the floor looking its best. We recommend a pH-neutral cleaner for routine cleaning.
Signs Your Epoxy Floor Needs Attention

Loss of gloss in high-traffic areas (the top coat is wearing, it can often be re-coated), scratches or scuffs (normal wear and tear, can be polished out or re-coated), and peeling or delamination (indicates a preparation failure, the floor needs professional assessment).
Our 10-Year Residential Warranty

We're confident enough in our installation quality to offer a 10-year Residential Warranty on all our epoxy flooring systems. This covers defects in materials and workmanship and gives you peace of mind that your floor is built to last. Read more about our warranty or request a free quote today. Call us on 07822 032335.

blocks.x: How to Prepare a Garage Floor for Epoxy Coating

If there's one thing that determines whether an epoxy floor will last for decades or fail within months, it's the preparation. Not the quality of the epoxy, not the skill of the application, the preparation. Here's what professional epoxy floor preparation involves and why it matters.
Why Preparation Matters

Epoxy doesn't stick to smooth concrete, it bonds to a properly prepared surface. Think of it like painting a glossy surface versus sanding it first. Without the right surface profile, the epoxy sits on top of the concrete rather than bonding into it. Eventually, the coating will peel, delaminate, or wear through prematurely. Proper preparation creates a mechanical bond that keeps the epoxy locked to the concrete for decades.
Step 1: Diamond Grinding

Diamond grinding is the gold standard for epoxy floor preparation. An industrial diamond grinding machine uses rotating discs embedded with diamond segments to abrade the concrete surface. This does two things: it removes any existing coatings, laitance (the weak surface layer of concrete), and contaminants, and it creates a surface profile, a slightly rough texture similar to medium-grit sandpaper, that the epoxy primer can grip into.

Diamond grinding is not something you can do with a handheld sander. Professional grinders weigh hundreds of kilograms and are connected to industrial vacuum systems to capture dust. The difference between a diamond-ground surface and an unprepared or poorly prepared surface is visible and measurable.
Our installation process always starts with diamond grinding, it's the foundation of every Rhino Coating floor.
Step 2: Crack and Defect Repair

Once the surface is ground, any cracks, spalling (where the concrete surface has broken away), or other defects become clearly visible. These must be repaired before coating. Cracks are chased out with a grinder to create a clean channel, then filled with a high-strength epoxy repair mortar. Expansion joints are treated with flexible sealants to allow movement. Loose or hollow areas of concrete are identified (often by tapping with a hammer) and addressed.
Skipping crack repair leads to the epoxy coating cracking along the same lines, the coating is only as strong as the substrate beneath it.
Step 3: Moisture Testing

Concrete contains moisture, it's porous and can wick water from the ground beneath. Before applying epoxy, we test the moisture content using a calibrated moisture meter and may also perform a calcium chloride test or relative humidity probe test for larger floors.

If moisture levels are too high, several solutions exist: applying a moisture-tolerant primer, installing a moisture vapour barrier, or in severe cases, addressing the source of moisture before proceeding. Ignoring this step means risking osmotic blistering, where moisture pressure pushes the coating off the concrete.
Step 4: Priming

Once the floor is ground, repaired, and confirmed dry, a primer coat is applied. The primer penetrates the surface profile, seals any remaining dust, and provides the ideal surface for the epoxy build coat to bond to. We use moisture-tolerant epoxy primers that can handle residual moisture levels that would cause problems for regular epoxy.

The primer is applied by squeegee and roller to ensure even coverage and worked into the surface profile. This step is often skipped in DIY applications, and it's one of the most important layers in the system.
What About Acid Etching?

Acid etching (using muriatic or phosphoric acid) is sometimes suggested as a DIY alternative to diamond grinding. While it does etch the surface, it's inconsistent, introduces moisture, requires careful neutralisation and rinsing, and doesn't create the same bond profile as mechanical grinding. It's also hazardous to handle. Professional installers do not rely on acid etching for epoxy flooring, diamond grinding is the standard for a reason.
The Rhino Coating Preparation Standard

Every floor we install goes through this complete preparation process, no shortcuts, no skipped steps. It's why our floors last 15-25+ years and why we confidently offer a 10-year residential warranty. If you're considering epoxy flooring and want it done properly, request a free quote or call us on 07822 032335.

blocks.x: Preparing for Your Installation
Rhino Coating Ltd, Company Registration Number: 16707536
Last updated: August 2026
Thank you for choosing Rhino Coating Ltd. To ensure your installation runs smoothly and your new floor achieves the highest possible finish, please take a few moments to read the guidance below.
Before We Arrive
To allow our installers to begin work immediately, please ensure that:
All vehicles are removed from the garage or work area before our arrival.
Shelving, storage units, toolboxes and personal belongings are removed wherever possible.
Any wall-mounted items that may be affected by dust are protected or removed.
A clear access route is available from our vehicle to the work area.
A standard electrical supply and access to water are available throughout the installation.
Children and pets are kept away from the work area at all times.
If you are unable to move heavy items, please let us know before your installation date so we can discuss suitable arrangements.
Existing Concrete
Our flooring systems are only as good as the surface they are applied to.
Although we carry out extensive preparation before installation, existing issues within the concrete may still become visible once preparation has begun.
Examples include:
Existing cracks.
Weak or damaged concrete.
Previous repairs.
Existing coatings or sealers.
Surface contamination.
Moisture-related issues.
If additional repairs are required beyond those included within your quotation, we will discuss the available options with you before proceeding.
During Installation
Our preparation process involves professional diamond grinding and industrial dust extraction equipment.
Whilst our systems significantly reduce airborne dust, customers should expect:
Some dust during preparation.
Noise from mechanical equipment.
Restricted access to the work area during installation.
For your safety, please do not enter the work area unless invited to do so by a member of our team.
After Installation
Your new floor requires time to cure before it reaches full strength.
Typical curing times are:
Light foot traffic: Approximately 24 hours.
Vehicle traffic: Approximately 72 hours.
Heavy equipment or point loading: As advised by Rhino Coating Ltd.
Please note that curing times may vary depending on temperature, humidity and site conditions.
Looking After Your New Floor
To achieve the best long-term performance:
Do not drag heavy objects across the floor.
Clean up oil, fuel and chemical spillages as soon as possible.
Use soft brushes or microfibre mops for routine cleaning.
Avoid abrasive cleaning products or harsh solvents unless recommended by Rhino Coating Ltd.
Follow the Aftercare & Maintenance Guide supplied with your installation.
Our Commitment
Every Rhino Coating floor is professionally prepared and installed using premium materials and industry-leading installation methods.
Our aim is to provide a floor that not only looks exceptional on the day of installation but continues to perform for many years to come.
If you have any questions before your installation, please don't hesitate to contact us. We're always happy to help.

8. Colour, Finish & Natural Characteristics

8.1 All product images, printed materials and colour samples are provided as a guide only. Due to manufacturing tolerances, application techniques, lighting conditions and digital screen variations, slight differences in colour, texture and finish may occur.

8.3 Resin flooring is a hand-finished decorative surface and every installation is unique. Minor variations are an inherent characteristic of the application process and are not considered defects.

8.4 These natural characteristics may include slight roller patterns, subtle texture variations, occasional pinholes, minor differences in sheen, decorative flake distribution and other small finish variations that do not affect the performance, durability or longevity of the flooring system.

10. Curing Times
10.1 Typical curing times are approximately 24 hours for foot traffic and 72 hours for vehicle traffic unless otherwise advised.
10.2 Heavy machinery or point loading should only be introduced following guidance from Rhino Coating Ltd.
10.3 Temperature and humidity may extend curing times.
11. Furniture & Vehicles
11.1 Heavy items and vehicles must not be placed on the floor until the advised curing period has elapsed.

13. Maintenance

13.2 Abrasive cleaners, wire brushes and unapproved solvents should not be used.
13.3 Failure to follow Rhino Coating Ltd's Aftercare Guide may invalidate the warranty.

14.1 Where provided, the warranty covers defects arising directly from Rhino Coating Ltd's workmanship and installation only.

14.2 The warranty does not cover structural movement, settlement, cracking of the substrate, moisture ingress, rising damp, hydrostatic pressure, impact damage, scratches, tyre staining, tyre plasticiser staining, chemical damage, flooding, fire, misuse, neglect, fair wear and tear, alterations by third parties or failure to follow the Aftercare Guide.

blocks.x: 10-Year Workmanship Warranty
Rhino Coating Ltd, Company Registration Number: 16707536
Last updated: August 2026

At Rhino Coating Ltd, we stand behind the quality of our workmanship and the care taken during every installation. Our 10-Year Workmanship Warranty has been designed to give you confidence that your new resin flooring system has been professionally installed.

This warranty applies to installations completed by Rhino Coating Ltd and is provided to the original purchaser. It is valid for 10 years from the date of practical completion, subject to the terms outlined below.
What is Covered
Subject to these Terms and Conditions, this warranty covers defects that arise solely as a direct result of Rhino Coating Ltd's workmanship during the installation process, including:
Loss of adhesion caused by installation defects.
Defects in workmanship.
Failure of the coating resulting directly from incorrect installation.
Delamination caused by installation where the concrete substrate was suitable at the time of installation.
Where a valid warranty claim is accepted, Rhino Coating Ltd will, at its discretion, repair or replace the affected area at no cost to the Customer.
What is Not Covered
This warranty does not cover defects or damage resulting from circumstances outside the control of Rhino Coating Ltd, including but not limited to:
Existing Substrate
Existing cracks within the concrete.
Future cracking or movement of the concrete slab.
Structural movement or settlement.
Weak, contaminated or defective concrete.
Existing moisture issues.
Rising damp or hydrostatic pressure.
Customer Damage
Impact damage.
Dragging heavy or sharp objects.
Accidental damage.
Misuse or neglect.
Incorrect cleaning methods.
Environmental Factors
Flooding.
Fire damage.
Chemical damage caused by prolonged exposure or misuse.
Damage caused by excessive heat outside the flooring system's intended use.
Normal Wear & Tear
Minor scratches.
Surface wear from normal use.
Tyre staining or tyre plasticiser marks.
Minor changes in gloss level over time.
Natural ageing of the flooring system.
Alterations
This warranty becomes void where the flooring has been altered, repaired or modified by any third party without the written approval of Rhino Coating Ltd.
Natural Characteristics
Resin flooring is a hand-finished decorative surface and every installation is unique.
Minor variations are an inherent characteristic of the application process and are not considered defects.

These natural characteristics may include slight roller patterns, subtle texture variations, occasional pinholes, minor differences in sheen, decorative flake distribution and other small finish variations that do not affect the performance, durability or longevity of the flooring system.

Every floor is individually installed by hand, meaning no two floors will ever be completely identical. These natural variations are a normal feature of professionally installed resin flooring and contribute to the unique appearance of each installation.
Customer Responsibilities
To maintain the validity of this warranty, the Customer agrees to:
Follow the Rhino Coating Ltd Aftercare & Maintenance Guide.
Clean the floor using suitable cleaning products.
Avoid dragging heavy objects across the floor.
Clean chemical spills promptly.
Allow the recommended curing period before use.
Failure to follow the recommended aftercare guidance may invalidate this warranty.
Making a Warranty Claim
If you believe your floor has developed a defect covered by this warranty, please contact Rhino Coating Ltd as soon as reasonably possible.
We may request photographs before arranging an inspection.

No third-party repairs or alterations should be carried out without first giving Rhino Coating Ltd reasonable opportunity to inspect the flooring and determine whether the issue is covered under this warranty.
Where a warranty claim is accepted, Rhino Coating Ltd reserves the right to repair, replace or otherwise remedy the affected area.
Our Commitment
We take great pride in every installation we complete.

Our reputation has been built on quality workmanship, premium materials and exceptional customer service. If an issue arises that is covered by this warranty, we will work with you to resolve it promptly, professionally and fairly.
Important Information

This is a workmanship warranty only. It does not guarantee against issues caused by the existing substrate, future movement, moisture, customer damage, misuse, wear and tear, environmental factors or third-party alterations.
This warranty applies only to the original installation carried out by Rhino Coating Ltd and is non-transferable unless agreed in writing.
This warranty is provided in addition to your statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. Nothing within this warranty limits or excludes those statutory rights.
